name: oauthlib-40b0ab56-blind27-ots
instr:
# OAuthLib giving wrong answers across its client and server flows — diagnosis without a test suite

This library is used on both sides of delegated access: by programs that go and ask a service for permission to act for a user, and by services that answer them. The repository has received 27 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the callers changed, yet the same calls that used to work now hand back wrong values, wrong statuses, or blow up where they used to answer.

Sending a person off to approve access is the first thing that goes wrong. Asking for a consent URL through the one-step helper that returns a URL together with a header map and an empty body, while passing an explicit set of scopes, gives back a URL with no scopes in it at all — the set handed in is thrown away and whatever the calling program already carries is used instead. The lower-level URL builder drops the handed-in scopes in the same way and independently, so repairing one place still leaves the other producing scopeless URLs; in that builder the redirect target, state, extra keyword fields and the proof-of-possession fields still come through as before. Deriving that proof-of-possession value from a freshly generated secret while naming no method no longer hands the secret back unchanged, and the method it records afterwards is not the plain one.
